title: TypeScript SDK — annotation-driven discriminator hints, progressive streaming parser, and zod-lite helpers for structured output
creator: Ava Morales
description:
Problem: Structured-output in streaming responses is fragile for polymorphic shapes. Current codegen emits full Zod schemas and union resolvers, but streaming-first scenarios often need (1) early routing based on a small discriminator token, (2) progressive parsing as more chunks arrive, and (3) a lighter runtime validator when we only validate partial shapes for latency-sensitive paths.

Proposal: Add an annotation-driven discriminator hint system plus a progressive parser runtime and a small 'zod-lite' helper runtime that can validate partial payloads and later hydrate into full Zod instances. The compiler will emit (a) JSDoc-like annotations on generated interfaces (e.g. @discriminator("kind", "KIND_") ), (b) a small shape-hints registry used by the streaming parser to route the incoming token stream to the correct partial parser, and (c) adapter glue to convert zod-lite results to full Zod validation on finalization.

Goals:
- Reduce first-byte routing latency for union responses by 30% in streaming mode.
- Avoid full-schema validation on every token boundary; enable progressive validation that accepts partial shapes and rejects only on finalization when necessary.
- Keep compatibility with existing TypeScript Zod users and existing JSON-Schema emitters.

Non-goals: Replace Zod entirely; solve every union-disambiguation case at compile time.

Design notes and rationale are below in implementation_notes and tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Generated client includes @discriminator annotations in emitted declarations and a shape-hints registry file (shape-hints.ts)
Streaming parser (stream-parser.ts) can use shape-hints to route the stream to a partial parser within 1 token on average for test corpus
zod-lite runtime exposes .partialParse(streamChunk) and .finalize() APIs and passes unit tests for partial acceptance/rejection semantics
End-to-end example: streaming chat API demonstration that shows early route selection and partial validation, published as examples/streaming-discriminator.md
Benchmarks show at least 20–30% reduction in median time-to-dispatch for routed union responses vs baseline full-parse approach
No regression on existing Zod-based validation test-suite; full validation path still supported and tested
implementation_notes: Codegen changes: add an optional @discriminator JSDoc tag on interfaces/unions. Example output: /** @discriminator('type','T_') */ export interface Dog { type: 'T_dog'; ... }
Emit shape-hints.ts with a minimal registry mapping: { 'T_': { key: 'type', values: ['T_dog','T_cat'], parserFactory: () => import('./parsers').dogPartialParser } }

Streaming runtime: stream-parser.ts will buffer up to N tokens to extract discriminator key (N default 3, configurable per-project). If a hint matches, it attaches the corresponding partial parser which implements a small state machine to validate incremental tokens.

zod-lite: a ~120KB minified runtime that implements a tiny subset of Zod necessary for structural checks (type guards, required keys, string/number enums). It supports partial parsing (marking fields as 'maybe present') and exposes hydrateToZod(fullSchema) to run final validation with the canonical Zod schema for strong guarantees.

Compatibility: generator still emits full Zod schemas (xxx.schema.ts) and JSON-Schema artifacts. zod-lite only used in streaming/latency paths; code paths for full validation continue to call the full Zod runtime.
Docs and examples: add examples/streaming-discriminator.md showing the client snippet and expected behavior; add migration notes for integrators who rely on union resolution ordering.
Telemetry: add opt-in feature flags to measure miss-rate (cases where shape-hints fail and fallback occurs) and token-sampling latency. Include metrics tags for model, route, and client-version.

Edge cases: ambiguous discriminators (overlapping prefixes) fall back to N-token buffered ambiguity resolver which uses heuristics + finalization to pick winner; ambiguous cases should be counted as misses in telemetry and flagged for future codegen improvements.
tasks: Spec: finalise annotation format and registry shape (owner: Luca)
Codegen: emit annotations and shape-hints.ts entries (owner: codegen team)
Runtime: implement stream-parser and zod-lite partial API (owner: runtime)
Adapters: glue code to hydrate zod-lite results into full Zod validation on finalize (owner: sdk)
Tests: unit tests for partial parsers, integration tests using mocked streaming responses (owner: qa)
Benchmarks: create benchmark harness and compare against baseline (owner: perf)
Docs: examples/streaming-discriminator.md and migration guide (owner: docs)
comments: 2025-01-16 - Ava Morales: Initial write-up and design sketch posted. Leaning toward prefix-based hints to keep runtime lookup cheap.
2025-01-22 - Luca Chen: Spike completed: prototype partial parser reduced route selection latency by ~28% on toy corpus. Uploaded prototype PR for early review (see linked_prs).
2025-01-27 - Design review (Maya Patel): UX considerations for examples: request auto-fallback should be explicit in client API and documented with code samples.
2025-02-02 - Security (R. Singh): Quick review — zod-lite runtime must not disable final strong validation by default. We should make zod-lite optional and opt-in per-route. Update planned.
2025-02-10 - Perf (J. Alvarez): Added benchmark harness; measured median dispatch improvement 24% on 512-sample corpus when using 2-token buffer for discriminator extraction.
2025-02-18 - Luca Chen: Merged shape-hints codegen prototype to feature branch. Next: integrate telemetry and finish unit tests.
